digest.component_or_area: LLM verifier model-class resolution across plan-review, completion, and code-review gates
propositions: Three verifier code paths select the model via an equality test against the default model, so any non-default (e.g. Bedrock or provider-qualified) model reads as an operator override and the downgrade to the standard class silently stops applying.

The fix routes all verifier paths through a single resolve_model_string function where trivial/standard/frontier are reserved class names resolved via class slots and any other string returns unchanged for back-compat.

The code-review.yaml verify step declares no model key and config.resolve_model does not call resolve_model_string, so code-review Pass-2 still runs on cfg.model (the frontier direct-Anthropic model) instead of the standard class even with a Bedrock class configured.

resolve_class always emits a provider-qualified id, breaking the promised byte-identical model string when no class is configured (bare claude-sonnet-4-6 becomes anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6), affecting usage logs and provenance.
The old contract letting an operator's explicit non-default model persist is the behavior this ticket intentionally removes; tests pinning that rule must be updated to the class-based contract.

Tests must exercise _verifier_cfg through its real callers at xcheck.py:198 and xcheck.py:336 with vacuous-pass guards, since isolated tests would stay green while a caller passing plain cfg leaves the verifier on the frontier model.
